messages:
Alice (support): FYI escalated from ACME — they hit a big tail latency spike after last night's quantization profile rollout. p95 stayed ~330ms but p99 jumped to ~1.8s for a subset of requests. Some requests timed out. Deploy id: qprof-v2 (rolled 2026-03-14T14:02Z).

Alice (support): Sample from customer: trace_id=acme-7f4d, request at 14:18 UTC. Repro steps they used included our standard text-generation endpoint + 1k tokens. They say it used to be stable.

deploy-bot: qprof-v2 applied to model redwood-13b@2026-03-14T14:02Z on cluster-dedicated-7 (rolling: 14:02 -> 14:08 UTC)

Ben (eng-runtime oncall): Noted. Can you paste the raw request/headers and the slow trace logs? Need: request body, route, model tag, and any inference logs (quantization/calibration messages). Also confirm whether this is hosted or dedicated for ACME.

Alice (support): ACME is on Dedicated (cluster-dedicated-7). Minimal repro here:

curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Account: acme" -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"Tell me a short story about a robot gardener","max_tokens":256,"temperature":0.2}'

Slow trace snippet from runtime logs (trimmed):
[14:18:05] request acme-7f4d start
[14:18:05] kv_cache: miss for prefix warm-up
[14:18:06] quant_calibration: starting dynamic calibration (samples=32)
[14:18:06] quant_calibration: heavy CPU work, blocking threads
[14:18:07] kernel_launch: fallback to fp16 for layers [10,11] (reason: calibration_out_of_range)
[14:18:08] inference_end latency_ms=1820

Alice (support): Customer reports ~20% of their requests in the past hour hit >1s, timeouts at 2s.

Priya (eng-ml): This looks like dynamic calibration triggering in the runtime. qprof-v2 enabled "dynamic_calibration: true" and aggressive fallback. If calibration encounters out-of-range activations it can either fallback to fp16 for affected layers or re-run calibration which blocks inference. That explains the single-request spikes (calibration is expensive + sometimes triggers fallback path).

Priya (eng-ml): Quick hypothesis: calibration samples include rare token sequences for this customer's prompts which push certain layer activation distributions outside the quantizer's expected range -> calibration logic stalls/waits and then runtime falls back.

Carlos (perf): Agreed. Two immediate mitigations:
1) short-term: route ACME traffic back to qprof-v1 (fp16) or force model variant to fp16 to stop dynamic calibration affecting production.
2) medium: disable dynamic calibration on dedicated clusters until we finish safety checks, or set calibration_samples to 8 and run offline calibration pre-warm.

Carlos (perf): Also suggest enabling "quantization.force_fp16_on_tail=true" for p99-sensitive tenants so tail work uses fp16 even if int8 is enabled for most requests. That reduces token CPU variance.

Ben (eng-runtime oncall): I'll do rollback routing for ACME now. Before I flip anything: what's the customer impact window and ETA expectations? Mina?

Mina (customer success): ACME has production traffic hitting the API — some user-facing features are degraded. They want an ETA within 30-60 min. Please prioritize.

Ben (eng-runtime oncall): Understood. Action plan: 1) roll ACME to qprof-v1 (fp16) via route override; 2) put a temporary guard that disables dynamic calibration for cluster-dedicated-7; 3) collect perf traces and microbenchmarks. I'll coordinate rollback and post status here.

Ben (eng-runtime oncall): Rolling traffic override ->
Command: `redwoodctl traffic set-route --account acme --model redwood-13b --variant qprof-v1 --cluster cluster-dedicated-7`

deploy-bot: traffic override applied for account=acme model=redwood-13b -> variant=qprof-v1 (applied 2026-03-14T15:02:21Z)

Ben (eng-runtime oncall): Also toggling dynamic calibration off on cluster-dedicated-7:
Command: `redwoodctl config set --cluster cluster-dedicated-7 --key quantization.dynamic_calibration --value false`

deploy-bot: config updated quantization.dynamic_calibration=false on cluster-dedicated-7 (15:05 UTC)

Ben (eng-runtime oncall): After override and toggle: preliminary numbers from ACME telemetry: p99 dropped from ~1.8s -> ~360ms within ~3 minutes. p95 unchanged at ~330ms.

Alice (support): ACME confirmed improved response times on their side and no more timeouts. They're appreciative but want root cause and a plan to re-enable int8 safely.

Priya (eng-ml): Next steps from ML side:
- Pull the calibration sample set used by qprof-v2 and run offline calibration with ACME's sample prompts to reproduce the out-of-range activations.
- Increase clip thresholds or adjust per-channel scaling to avoid out-of-range fallback.
- Consider an offline pre-calibration pass for dedicated clusters with tenant samples.

Carlos (perf): I'll run microbenchmarks w/ variants: int8 (dynamic_calibration on), int8 (dynamic_calibration off), int8 (force_fp16_on_tail), fp16. Will measure p50/95/99 and memory/CPU. Expectation: dynamic_calibration off + occasional scheduled offline calibration should give most of int8 cost wins without tail spikes.

Ben (eng-runtime oncall): Data/telemetry requests for follow-up:
- sample traces where quant_calibration triggered (we need stack traces and timestamps)
- kernel fallback reasons and layer ids
- distribution of activation magnitudes for the layers that fell back
- account routing logs showing which variant served each request

Please upload to the incident folder and tag @eng-ml and @perf.

Carlos (perf): I'll push a benchmark PR and post results to this thread when done. If we see reproducible per-layer issues, we can introduce a safety check: if calibration would trigger fallback for >2 layers, treat profile as unsafe and keep fp16 for that tenant automatically.

Priya (eng-ml): Agreed. Also let's add a telemetry flag to mark requests that triggered calibration so we can correlate prompts.

Mina (customer success): I'll send ACME a summary and ETA for re-enabling int8 (target: validate in 48h). They want a rollback ticket and a postmortem.

Ben (eng-runtime oncall): Status update 15:50 UTC: rollback override still active, dynamic_calibration=false on the cluster, ACME p99 back to ~340ms. Monitoring for 30m. Leaving this thread open for follow-ups (perf numbers, calibration artifacts).

Alice (support): Thanks team. Action items captured:
- Ben: maintain override and monitor (done)
- Priya: run offline calibration with ACME corpus, push fixes to calibration logic
- Carlos: perf benchmarks and PR for safety rule
- Mina: customer comms + postmortem draft

Ben (eng-runtime oncall): If anyone needs to test toggles: quick config examples below:

# recommended temporary config to avoid tail spikes
{
  "quantization.mode": "int8",
  "quantization.dynamic_calibration": "false",
  "quantization.fallback_to_fp16": "true",
  "quantization.force_fp16_on_tail": "true",
  "quantization.calibration_samples": "8"
}

Ben (eng-runtime oncall): Will post perf numbers and calibration artifacts when available. Closing this escalation once we have postmortem and safe re-enable plan. :white_check_mark:
